old_capture_is_evidence_of: the foreign window that occupied the rectangle, never of the COS Desktop window

repair.capture: PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT) on the target HWND only; any failure is a closed NOT_MEASURED refusal, never a fallback image.
repair.content: A 7x7 sampled grid of the bound capture must agree with the display over the window's on-screen region (>= 45/49 samples within 24 RGB levels); the capture must also be non-blank (>= 4 distinct sampled colours, >= 45 non-black samples). The target is briefly raised topmost without activation for the comparison and restored immediately; both are recorded. A foreign window on top makes the sampled agreement fail.
repair.identity: The record carries the capture method, HWND, pid, title, the rectangle at capture and still_current; the harness re-queries the HWND itself (IsWindow, GetWindowThreadProcessId, GetWindowTextW, GetWindowRect) before the application is stopped.
repair.labels: Every expected Latin surface label and the Japanese fixture title must be present in the UI Automation tree; a missing label fails the run.

replacement.note: The replacement image was opened and visually confirmed to be the COS Desktop window during this repair.

reviewer_finding.confirmed_here: The stored PNG was opened again during MP-TYP1-C-R1 and is a foreign web page, not the shell window.
reviewer_finding.summary: The saved screenshot is not the COS Desktop window; it shows a foreign Chinese video web page. Its PNG size, byte count and sha256 matched the record, so the hash was right and the content was wrong.

root_cause.capture: apps/desktop/devtools/r0/n03_probe.ps1 captured Graphics.CopyFromScreen over the window rectangle, unbound to the target HWND; whatever window occupied the rectangle (here a fullscreen video player) was recorded as this window.
root_cause.verification: apps/desktop/devtools/typography/host_observe.py only compared PNG dimensions with the window rectangle, which cannot detect foreign content.
